_doc: Thủy Vân's eight peoples (ThuyVanCanon.people). Public fields only: what a traveller in Book I could know. Every row: id, src (bible ids), status (canon: the bible's or the owner's word; proposal: the lead's placeholder until the owner signs it off; owner_pick: waiting for the owner to choose).
proposal_fields names the fields of a canon row that are still proposals. Display strings are {text, voice}; voice is ui, narration, npc, notice or imperial.

name: the bible's English name (the primary label). title: the English title shown beside it. vi_candidates: the Vietnamese names offered to the owner; shown stays 'pending' until he picks (no Hán characters in game).

homeland: atlas ids. body_kit: human (the Actor_B body as it is), extension (Actor_B plus extension bones or added geometry), new (a body of its own). playable_wave: the order the peoples become playable (1 first). Ancestor-Bound is a human lineage with a Bound or Unbound condition, not a body.
name_format: how a full name is put together ({given}, {family}, {clan}, {house}, {mooring}, {channel}, {grove}); naming says it in words.

title.text: Dragon-Sea People, People of the Estuaries

naming.text: Family name first, then the given name; titles such as Lieutenant or Admiral are earned and go before the name.

line.text: They work the delta's locks, boats and salt pans, and their court houses say the rivers answer to one line.

title.text: Mountain Folk, People of the High Places

naming.text: One or two syllables, given with the clan, as in "<name> of <clan>"; an office such as Mother of Fire is a form of address, not a name.

line.text: Hill clans of terraces, goats and oath-stones, who will quarrel over a pass toll and still carry a stranger down in a storm.

title.text: Stone Children, of the Stone Valleys

naming.text: Two syllables with a craft or mineral sense, given with the guild house, as in "<name> of House <house>".

line.text: Heavy, careful builders from the Stone Valleys, who sign the joints of every bridge they raise.

naming.text: Hard syllables, often joined by a hyphen, given with the mooring, as in "<name> of <mooring> Mooring".

line.text: The marsh people of the Reed Marches; the toll officers call them raiders, and they call the marshes theirs.

naming.text: Short names, given with the channel whose rights the family keeps, as in "<name> of <channel>".

line.text: River families who keep their own channels and licences, and lately send no guides to the imperial piers.

naming.text: A public name, a contracted name and a private name; a stranger is only ever given the public one.

line.text: Brokers and keepers of witnessed bargains, said to know the worth of every promise.

naming.text: Names that carry the grove's Mộc, given with the grove, as in "<name> of <grove>".

line.text: Forest folk of bark and root, seldom seen beyond the shade of their own groves.

naming.text: Vietnamese names given with the house, as in "<name> of House <house>"; shrine titles such as Father, Sister or Novice go before the name.

line.text: Shrine households who keep the names of their dead, and some of whom hear those dead answer.
